prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1191; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver was named on the policy as a person who may NOT drive the car.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in a traffic lane in Pearland, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2. The damage to Driver 1's vehicle is largely in line with an impact of this kind, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known to the responding officer. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat and reported pain in the right shoulder. Officers and two independent witnesses confirmed that Passenger was inside the vehicle at the time. The shoulder complaint fits the forward and rearward motion described at the scene. Witnesses, scene photographs and Driver 2's own account all agree on how the collision happened. Driver 1 is listed on the policy as a person who may not operate the vehicle, a point noted for the insurer's review. No citations were issued at the scene while the investigation continues.
